item.title: Local service says instances of domestic abuse rise during Christmas
item.description: While we often picture Christmas as a time for laughter and special moments with family, the reality can be a lot different for those living with domestic abuse. That's according to Siobhan McKenna from the Tearmann Domestic Support Service for Cavan and Monaghan. Siobhan says instances of domestic abuse often rise during this time of year. item.title: Cavan vet warns pet owners to keep eye out on toxic foods this Christmas
item.description: Local pet owners should 'act swiftly' if an animal ingests Christmas treats over the festive period. Aoife Flanagan, a vet with the Cavan vet clinic says that there are a number of things this time of year that are toxic for animals. She says that if foods are not usually in a pet's diet they should not be given to them at Christmas or the New Year, as they could cause gastric issues. item.title: Bereaved families reminded to acknowledge their grief this festive period
item.description: People are being reminded to acknowledge their grief over the festive period. The Irish Hospice Foundation is advising people to take care of themselves and those around them who may have been recently bereaved. item.title: Man dies in Christmas Day collision between car and e-scooter
item.description: A man has died following a road traffic collision involving a car and an e-scooter in Waterford city on Christmas Day. The crash happened at the junction of Manor Hill, and Hennessy’s Road at around 11:00 am. The e-scooter rider, a man in his 40s, was taken to University Hospital Waterford where he was later pronounced dead. item.description: "Most fatalities that take place throughout the year could be avoided." That's according to Adrian O'Sullivan who is the road safety officer with Monaghan County Council. item.title: Kingscourt woman says homelessness crisis is getting worse
item.description: A Kingscourt woman who feeds hundreds of homeless people in Dublin each week says things have only got worse. Sonya McMahon from 'Help Our Homeless' run by her and her family offer food to the homeless in the city 365 days a year. She feeds up on 200 people twice a week outside the GPO along with a outreach service seven days a week visiting tents in parks and beaches in the harder to reach areas across the capital. item.title: Locals urged to ensure homes are equipped with working fire alarms
item.description: Monaghan's Chief Fire Officer, Dermot Brannigan has advised locals to ensure that they have a working fire alarm in place this Christmas. Speaking to Shannonside Northern Sound, Mr Brannigan said that a fire alarm is the only method of early detection should a fire break out. With an increase in households set to light fires at home over the festive period, Mr Brannigan has also encouraged people to clean their chimneys and ensure that you have a fire guard. item.title: Mary Slowey (nee Gaffey)
item.description: Mary Slowey (nee Gaffey) Drumalee, Cavan Town. Mary died on Friday December 26th 2025 (St.Stephen's Day), peacefully in the loving care of her family and the staff at Cavan General Hospital, in her 97th year. Predeceased by her beloved husband Tommie, her son Sean and her infant daughter Bernadette.
